ctx.x: Well, I'm telling you now, Rene, myself, Buddy Petit be somewhere, Chris Kelly be somewhere. And different bands, you know like that.
What about the white bands? Did they have white bands out there?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: I won two Cups, one at the Espinade Hall down there, against Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: Who did you meet in the street, some of the different bands?

Well, every Sunday you'd meet a bunch, but it'd be the same bunch like Rene, Buddy Petit, Sam Marock, Chris Kelly, and what's his name? The Dine, downtown there, Cindy Desvinge, the old tuxedo, all them bands used to be out on the street, you know, advertising dances on Sundays. Maybe one of them would be playing at a funeral or something, somebody would die, and they'd all get on that together.
Did you ever have any battles of music in the places like, say, the Bows Club or any of those?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What about Chris Kelly? [INTERVIEWEE] Well, Chris was a nice man with a plunger, you know. He was a plunger man.

ctx.x: Well, let me get out my little notebook again, Punch, and we'll go back and I'll ask you about some of the different people and bands you work with, stuff like that. I wanted to ask you more about the different styles of the trumpet players they had here. Like, how would you describe Buddy Petit's style?

Well, I'm telling you, he had a wonderful style of playing at home. He wasn't a high note man, but he was, he had a wonderful tone and played everything clean. Real clean trumpet player. He was. Rene, he was a high note man. He went up in the air all the time. Ricard was turning out to be a nice trumpet player too until he got hype. Ricard was getting all right. What about Chris Kelly?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Well, in my time, there was Buddy Petit, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, Ricard, Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and them.

ctx.x: And what's your name, Paul? Paul Crawford. Dick Allen is my name. So, we got everybody's name here. All right. Now, I guess I wanted to talk to you about trumpet playing, particularly in the old days. Who were some of the outstanding trumpet players you heard when you were young?

Well, in my time, there was Buddy Petit, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, Ricard, Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and them. Of course, King Oliver and them were those brothers. King Oliver and Louis Criddy Kepert and them kind of fellas. Another fella by the name of Shatz.
He was older than you or your age?
